- (1) Patch anchors apply byte-for-byte: include block OLD matches lv2_register.c:25-29; SPU_LS_SIZE block OLD matches :714-717; materialize block OLD matches :350-353; image_open hdr[52]/fread/fclose+entry parse OLD matches :960-973.

- (6) Test links the REAL spu_elf.c, builds BE EM_SPU ELF32 with memsz>filesz, poisons LS 0xAA, asserts bytes@vaddr/BSS zeroed/neighbors/count/entry + truncated+wrong-machine rejects. runtime/spu/tests/ exists with identical standalone-.c pattern, excluded by CMake /tests/ filter; runtime/spu/spu_elf.c picked up by runtime/*.c GLOB (CMakeLists.txt:44-55) automatically.

THE BUG (now fixed in patches): PATCH 2 placed typedef spu_image_cache_t and spu_image_cache_find() at line 714, but PATCH 3 USES them at ~:350 (360 lines earlier). C has no forward visibility => compile failure (unknown type / implicit declaration). The existing :350 call to spu_thread_get_or_alloc_ls only works because of an explicit forward decl at :245. FIX: move the cache block to right after the forward-decl region (:246), before sys_spu_thread_initialize_handler. SECOND related bug: SPU_LS_SIZE is #defined at :717 (after :350), so using it at :350 is undeclared; added PATCH 2b moving the #define up.

MINOR (non-blocking, corrected in test): original save/restore of e_machine saved only the high byte; the "6 checks" label undercounts the 7 CHECK calls. Cosmetic; corrected to 7 and to a clean put_be16(elf+18,0x0099).
risks:
1) BLOCKING (now fixed): original PATCH 2 defined spu_image_cache_t / spu_image_cache_find at :714 but PATCH 3 used them at ~:350 — a C forward-reference error that would NOT compile. Corrected by relocating the cache block to just after the forward-decl region (:246), before sys_spu_thread_initialize_handler.

2) BLOCKING-adjacent (now fixed): PATCH 3 references SPU_LS_SIZE at ~:350, but it is #defined at :717 (after the handler). Original design overlooked this; added PATCH 2b moving the #define up. Without it the build fails 'SPU_LS_SIZE undeclared'.

3) Ownership/leaks: store() takes ownership; handler nulls fbuf after cache, frees otherwise; bounded 64; same-key replace frees prior; full => drop+free (no leak, falls back to legacy). No process-teardown free (acceptable; matches s_spu_threads lifetime).

4) img_ea reuse: keyed by img_ea, replace-on-key; spu_image_materialize keeps priority so the cached-ELF path never overrides a real materialized image. Matches PS3 per-image open.

5) entry override: cached path sets t->entry_point=e_entry only when a segment loaded; equals image_open's img_ea+4 value (:976) for project images => no regression; ELF e_entry wins when they differ (intended).

6) Include path "../spu/spu_elf.h" resolves from runtime/syscalls/; no CMake edit (GLOB + exclusions verified). spu_elf.c auto-compiled into ps3recomp_runtime.

7) wrap_spu_elf.py emits p_filesz==p_memsz (no BSS), so a wrap()-made ELF never tests zero-fill — exactly why the unit test hand-builds memsz>filesz. Honest gap closed by the test, not by reusing wrap().

8) Minor (corrected): original test's e_machine save/restore saved only the high byte; "6 checks" label undercounted. Both cosmetic; fixed. Neither affected pass/fail.
